description.narrative: The Indonesia Infrastructure and Finance Compact, which will include a $49 million contribution from the Government of Indonesia in addition to the $649 million of MCC grant funding, seeks to assist the Government of Indonesia in tackling these issues by addressing a binding constraint to the country's economic growth: costly and underdeveloped financial intermediation�or access to financing. The compact will specifically focus on improving the financing of infrastructure�particularly transport and logistics infrastructure�and increasing access to finance for MSMEs through three projects.

condition.narrative: Before any Disbursement of Program Funding on or after the commencement of year five (5) of the Compact Term, MCA-Indonesia II must submit to MCC an initial draft Closure Plan in accordance with the MCC Policy on Program Closure.

Before each Disbursement of Program Funding for payment under a particular works or construction contract for a given Project or Activity, MCA-Indonesia II must submit evidence, in form and substance satisfactory to MCC, that MCA-Indonesia II or the appropriate Government entity is implementing the requirements of each ESIA, ESMP, HSMP, or RAP, as appropriate, for such Project or Activity in all material respects and consistent with the Environmental Guidelines (including the IFC Performance Standards that are incorporated by reference therein).

Before the first Disbursement of Program Funding for any activity to be carried out under an implementing entity arrangement, MCA-Indonesia II must deliver to MCC a copy of a signed agreement between MCA-Indonesia II and the relevant Implementing Entity that sets forth the roles and responsibilities of each party with respect to the applicable Project or Activity, which agreement must be in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.

Before the first Disbursement of Program Funding for payment under a particular works or construction contract for a given Project or Activity, MCA-Indonesia II must submit evidence, in form and substance satisfactory to MCC, that MCA-Indonesia II or the appropriate Government entity has developed and adopted an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment or ESIA, an Environmental and Social Management Plan or ESMP, a Health and Safety Management Plan or HSMP, and/or a Resettlement Action Plan or RAP (as appropriate) for such Project or Activity, each of which must be in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.

Before the first Disbursement of Program Funding that occurs 180 days after the Compact enters into force, MCA-Indonesia II must develop and adopt a comprehensive M&E Plan, in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.
Before the first Disbursement of Program Funding, MCA-Indonesia II must develop and adopt an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS).
Before the second Disbursement of Program Funding, MCA-Indonesia II must develop and adopt a comprehensive Social and Gender Integration Plan, in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.
Each of the Key Staff has been selected and engaged by MCA-Indonesia II and approved by MCC.

MCA-Indonesia II has been legally established and the Government has provided MCC with copies of all decrees, legislations, or other documents relating to the establishment of MCA-Indonesia II and its operations (including the Bylaws and HR Manual).
MCA-Indonesia II has delivered to MCC a completed Disbursement Request covering the related Disbursement Period in accordance with the QDRP Guidance.
MCA-Indonesia II has developed a Fiscal Accountability Plan (or an interim version), and the plan has been approved by MCC.
MCA-Indonesia II has developed and adopted the HR Manual, and the manual has been approved by MCC
MCA-Indonesia II has developed the Procurement and Grants Plan Package (or an interim version), and the plan has been approved by MCC.

MCC has determined in its discretion that MCA-Indonesia II has complied in all material respects with its obligations set forth in PIA �2.1(d) with respect to the establishment of a Bid Challenge System.

MCC has determined in its discretion that MCA-Indonesia II has made progress, satisfactory to MCC, on implementing the Projects or Activities for which funding is requested, including progress on each of the Principal Implementation Plans
MCC has determined in its discretion that MCC does not have grounds for concluding that any matter certified to it in any certificate provided as part of the Disbursement Request is not as certified.

MCC has determined in its discretion that all Government entities involved in the implementation of the Program, including the Implementing Entities, are coordinating successfully with MCA-Indonesia II and dedicating the necessary staff and other resources to ensure successful implementation of the Program.

MCC has determined in its discretion that any Taxes paid with MCC Funding through the date 90 days prior to the start of the related Disbursement Period have been reimbursed by the Government in full in accordance with �2.8(c) of the Compact.
MCC has determined in its discretion that each of the Key Staff remains engaged, or if a position is vacant, MCA-Indonesia II is actively engaged, to MCC�s satisfaction, in recruiting a replacement.

MCC has determined in its discretion that no act, omission, condition, or event has occurred that would be the basis for MCC to suspend or terminate, in whole or in part, the Compact or MCC Funding in accordance with �5.1 of the Compact.

MCC has determined in its discretion that no material default or breach of any covenant, obligation, or responsibility by the Government, MCA-Indonesia II, or any Government entity, has occurred and is continuing under the Compact, this Agreement, or any other Supplemental Agreement.

MCC has determined in its discretion that the Government has complied in all material respects with its obligations set forth in PIA �2.8 with respect to the making of its contributions in accordance with the projected timeline set forth in PIA Annex III.

MCC has determined in its discretion that the Government has satisfied all of its payment obligations, including any insurance, indemnification, tax payments or other obligations, and contributed all resources required from it, under the Compact, this Agreement, and any other Supplemental Agreement.

MCC has determined in its discretion that the M&E Plan is current and updated and MCA-Indonesia II is in substantial compliance with the requirements of the M&E Plan (including any applicable reporting requirements set forth therein for the related Disbursement Period).
MCC has determined in its discretion that the activities to be funded with such Disbursement shall not violate any applicable law or regulation

MCC has determined in its discretion that there has been no material negative finding in any financial audit report delivered in accordance with the Compact and Audit Plan, for the prior two quarters (or such other period as the Audit Plan may require).
The Compact has entered into force as provided in Article 7 of the Compact.
